title: Staying Put
summary: New scheduled tasks on two computers. One came with a printer driver IT pushed out. The other came from a script someone opened - and it brought a way to come back every time they sign in.
story: You are the analyst on shift at {{CO}} (a made-up company). Intruders don't want to break in twice, so after getting in they set up a way to start again by themselves: a program in the registry's Run key, a scheduled task, a service. Installers do the same thing for honest reasons. The rule "New scheduled task" fired on two computers.
goal: Decide which alert is real, then trace it: the account, the file that was opened, when it started, the Run key value and the scheduled task it left, and the address it calls home to.
skills: persistence (Run keys, scheduled tasks), process trees, beacon timing in firewall logs

questions.ask: The "New scheduled task" alert on WS-{{HA}}: real attack or false alarm? (one try)
questions.explain: On {{GOODH}} the task was made by the Inkwell printer driver's installer, run as SYSTEM by the deployment tool, pointing into Program Files. On {{BADH}} it was made by a program downloaded seconds earlier by a script from a zip file.

questions.ask: Which account was signed in on the attacked computer?
Which file did the person open that started it all?
questions.explain: wscript.exe's cmdline: a script inside a downloaded zip.

questions.ask: At what time (HH:MM:SS) was it opened?
Which value was added to the registry's Run key (its name)?
What is the scheduled task it created called (without the backslash)?
Which outside address does it call home to?
questions.explain: The download came from it, and the firewall shows a connection to it every five minutes since.

hints.text: Compare who made each task: siem search source=proclog image=*schtasks* shows the parent of each schtasks.exe. Then follow the bad one's family upwards (what started its parent?) until you reach the first program.

The program that set up the tasks also used reg.exe. Its cmdline shows the Run key value. For calling home, siem search source=firewall src=ADDRESS --count-by dst shows where the computer connects again and again; no DNS lookup is needed when a program uses a bare address.
